plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the low-speed limit or when the nonlinear drag coefficient tends to zero, so resistance is effectively proportional to omega alone.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes rotational resistance is exactly linear in angular velocity over the full admissible speed range, omitting the common increase of drag strength with speed.
plan.baseline_assumption: Rotational resistance is linear in angular velocity.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Nonlinear rotational drag from aerodynamic losses or turbulent bearing/shear effects that grow faster than linearly with angular speed.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the exact linear-drag assumption rather than add an unrelated new state. Hold rotor_inertia and resistance parameters fixed, and vary the constant drive_torque so trajectories reach different speed ranges under the same observation protocol and initial condition. In the parent, all runs collapse onto the same straight domega_dt-versus-omega line with one shared slope, so changing drive_torque only shifts the intercept. In the child, that line bends downward at larger |omega| because resistance grows faster with speed, changing the target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. This is scientifically admissible for a rigid rotor at sufficiently high rotational speed where fluid drag or internal dissipation becomes nonlinear, yet still below any structural or thermal breakdown. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot match both the near-origin slope and the stronger high-speed braking across multiple torque conditions, because its affine omega dependence fixes curvature to zero.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, higher-speed portions of the trajectory already show mild mid-course bending from warm-up; in holdout, longer or stronger-drive runs extend this same history-dependent curvature and lower terminal speed, rather than introducing a qualitatively different mechanism.

plan.promotion_reason: A fixed resistance_coefficient cannot encode history-dependent warm-up within one run. To make dissipation-induced drift observable in the scored target mapping, the resistance level itself must evolve as a state rather than remain a constant parameter.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes rotational resistance responds instantaneously to speed and remains time-invariant during a run, omitting self-heating of bearings/lubricant or windage environment that can change resistance as the rotor dissipates power.
plan.baseline_assumption: The linear resistance coefficient is constant in time and independent of the rotor's dissipative history.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Dissipation-driven thermal conditioning changes the effective viscous rotational resistance during the experiment, producing history-dependent drag and altered relaxation curvature.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-resistance assumption rather than add an unrelated torque term, because the parent already contains resistance but idealizes it as time-invariant. Vary the within-run elapsed time and reachable speed under fixed drive_torque, rotor_inertia, nonlinear_drag_coefficient, and speed_transition. In the parent, domega_dt is determined solely by current omega through one static drag curve. In the child, dissipation during spin-up changes the effective resistance coefficient, so two times in a run with the same omega can have different domega_dt after different accumulated heating. The contrast is admissible when heating is appreciable over the observed interval; if dissipation is too small or thermal equilibration is extremely fast to a nearly constant value, the effect may be weak and the parent becomes an adequate approximation. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the early cold-start slope and the later warmed stronger curvature across such conditions, because its drag curve is fixed for all times within the run.

plan.activation_condition: Visible when dissipative heating is strong enough to create non-negligible excess_drag and the cooling environment changes over times comparable to the experiment, so that cooling_time_constant is not effectively constant during the sampled trajectory.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate heating already reveals that slower versus faster cooling changes the curvature of resistance_coefficient recovery and thus domega_dt transients; in holdout, stronger heating extends the same interaction and exposes larger separation in spin-up and relaxation without changing the mechanism.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the cooling-effectiveness state is clamped constant, equivalently in the limit of infinitely fast relaxation of that state to a fixed nominal cooling_time_constant or zero coupling from dissipation to cooling.
plan.promotion_reason: A fixed cooling_time_constant enforces a fixed thermal environment. To model heat-soak or ventilation degradation during a run, cooling effectiveness must evolve dynamically; existing states cannot represent this environmental memory without overloading their physical meanings.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes thermal recovery occurs with a fixed time constant even during prolonged dissipation, omitting the realistic possibility that the surroundings and lubricant become heat-soaked so cooling efficiency itself changes during the experiment.
plan.baseline_assumption: The parent assumes the cooling_time_constant is constant throughout the run.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Environment/lubricant heat soak modifies heat removal efficiency, making the relaxation timescale of the fast resistance conditioning evolve with dissipative loading and recovery history.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-environment assumption behind thermal recovery. In the parent, domega_dt changes only through omega and the two drag states, with cooling entering resistance_coefficient dynamics through one constant timescale. Vary the dissipative loading along the observed trajectory by letting omega rise under fixed drive_torque while holding all other fixed parameters shared across runs. Then compare trajectories that spend substantial time at high heating_power_proxy versus those that do not. Physically, sustained dissipation can warm the housing, bearings, lubricant, or nearby air, reducing heat extraction and increasing the effective cooling_time_constant during the same run. That creates an interaction: the same instantaneous excess_drag produces different subsequent recovery slopes depending on the cooling state reached by prior heating. This changes the target mapping indirectly but observably, because domega_dt depends on resistance_coefficient, whose transient level and persistence are altered by evolving cooling. The parent with one shared fixed cooling_time_constant can shift all recovery rates uniformly, but cannot reproduce both early-time and late-time curvature when cooling degrades during high-load portions and later recovers. The refinement is admissible when heating is strong enough and the experiment lasts long enough for cooling efficiency to drift; if heating remains weak or observation windows are short, the added effect may be hard to distinguish.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping uses drag coefficients conditioned only by internally generated dissipation, so for fixed observed omega and resistance_coefficient the angular acceleration is independent of ambient heat-removal state.
response_change.child_relation: Release cooling_time_constant as a slowly evolving state representing environment-dependent cooling effectiveness, so the target mapping acquires a history-dependent interaction between omega, resistance_coefficient, and the cooling state through altered resistance buildup and decay.
response_change.observable_effect: Under equal drive_torque and identical initial omega, runs entering a weak-cooling regime show slower drag recovery after heating and therefore a more prolonged reduction in domega_dt during spin-up and relaxation than a strong-cooling regime; one shared parent parameter set with fixed cooling cannot match both transient curvature patterns.

diagnostic_groups.name: heating_power_proxy
diagnostic_groups.role: Current dissipative loading that thermally conditions drag

diagnostic_groups.name: excess_drag
diagnostic_groups.role: Fast thermal elevation of effective viscous resistance above the drifting baseline

contract.activation_condition: Visible when dissipative heating is strong enough to create non-negligible excess_drag and the cooling environment changes over times comparable to the experiment, so that cooling_time_constant is not effectively constant during the sampled trajectory.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate heating already reveals that slower versus faster cooling changes the curvature of resistance_coefficient recovery and thus domega_dt transients; in holdout, stronger heating extends the same interaction and exposes larger separation in spin-up and relaxation without changing the mechanism.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the cooling-effectiveness state is clamped constant, equivalently in the limit of infinitely fast relaxation of that state to a fixed nominal cooling_time_constant or zero coupling from dissipation to cooling.
contract.promotion_reason: A fixed cooling_time_constant enforces a fixed thermal environment. To model heat-soak or ventilation degradation during a run, cooling effectiveness must evolve dynamically; existing states cannot represent this environmental memory without overloading their physical meanings.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Environment/lubricant heat soak modifies heat removal efficiency, making the relaxation timescale of the fast resistance conditioning evolve with dissipative loading and recovery history.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the cooling state enters through a nonlinear heating-driven degradation term and then feeds back inside the denominator of the resistance relaxation law, creating history-dependent transient curvature rather than a uniform rescaling.
contract.assumption_before: The parent assumes the cooling_time_constant is constant throughout the run.
contract.assumption_after: Cooling effectiveness evolves dynamically under dissipative heat soak and recovery, so cooling_time_constant becomes an internal state.
contract.before_fragment: (drive_torque - resistance_coefficient * omega - nonlinear_drag_coefficient * (1 + thermal_drag_sensitivity * (resistance_coefficient - baseline_resistance_coefficient) / (thermal_drag_scale + Abs(resistance_coefficient - baseline_resistance_coefficient))) * omega**3 / (speed_transition + Abs(omega))) / rotor_inertia
contract.after_fragment: (drive_torque - resistance_coefficient * omega - nonlinear_drag_coefficient * (1 + thermal_drag_sensitivity * (resistance_coefficient - baseline_resistance_coefficient) / (thermal_drag_scale + Abs(resistance_coefficient - baseline_resistance_coefficient))) * omega**3 / (speed_transition + Abs(omega))) / rotor_inertia
contract.parent_reduction: Set cooling_heat_sensitivity = 0 and initialize cooling_time_constant = nominal_cooling_time_constant with nominal_cooling_time_constant equal to the parent fixed cooling_time_constant, or take cooling_recovery_time_constant sufficiently small that cooling_time_constant remains effectively clamped to nominal_cooling_time_constant.
contract.observable_signature: Compared at equal drive_torque and shared initial conditions, trajectories with substantial heating_power_proxy develop larger cooling_time_constant, which slows excess-drag recovery and produces delayed curvature changes in resistance_coefficient and hence longer-lived suppression of domega_dt; under weak heating the child collapses back toward parent-like behavior.
contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent parameters with one fixed cooling_time_constant can only impose one recovery-rate law for resistance_coefficient across the run. It cannot reproduce the within-trajectory shift from faster early recovery to slower late recovery caused by heat-soak-induced growth of cooling_time_constant, nor match both weak-heating and strong-heating transient curvature patterns with a single shared parameter set.

range_suggestions.cooling_time_constant: positive; initially near nominal_cooling_time_constant and allowed to increase above it during prolonged heating, with changes occurring on timescales comparable to or slower than resistance_coefficient relaxation
range_suggestions.cooling_heat_sensitivity: positive, typically small enough that cooling degradation is gradual over a run
range_suggestions.cooling_recovery_time_constant: positive, often comparable to or larger than cooling_time_constant so environmental heat soak recovers slowly
range_suggestions.nominal_cooling_time_constant: positive, near the parent fixed cooling_time_constant reference
